title: Cairnfire
brief: A dramatic concert overture for full orchestra, four to five minutes: a stark opening gesture, a driving figure in the low strings with timpani and brass over it, a broad singing theme in the middle heard as from a good seat in the hall, a development with a fugato, and the opening returning at full force to land. Written for the sections, not for soloists.

sections.intent: The opening gesture: a bare E, B rising to C, the augmented sixth, a bare B, silence
The driving figure in cellos and basses with timpani; the first theme in the horns, then the full orchestra
The figure thins; woodwinds turn the gesture toward G major; the tempo broadens
The singing theme in G major: first violins, then violins and cellos in octaves to its peak
The singing theme in B flat major by the whole orchestra, to its highest note
A deceptive cadence into G minor; the theme in the minor falls into the gesture's turn
Fugato on the gesture: violas, second violins, cellos and basses, first violins; an episode
The subject's head in imitation in the brass, the singing theme in F, the augmented sixth
The dominant pedal: the figure returns, the turn climbs, everything swells
The opening at full force; the first theme by the whole orchestra, extended to the dominant
Faster: tonic pedal, the themes compressed, Neapolitan cadences, and the bare E to end

decisions: Key E minor; 4/4; Allegro con fuoco at 140, the singing theme at 90, the coda at 150. 133 bars.

One cell runs through the piece: the fifth above the tonic, the note above it, the note below it, and back (B, C, A sharp, B). It is the opening gesture, the upper line of the low strings' figure, the head of the fugato subject, the climbing turn over the dominant pedal and the close of the coda; harmonised, it is the augmented sixth C-E-G-A sharp resolving to B.
The opening is bare octaves and silence, no chord until the augmented sixth: stark by having no third.

The singing theme is given to the string sections (first violins; then violins and cellos in octaves; then violins in octaves with flutes and oboes), never to a solo string instrument. Its second statement is a minor third higher, in B flat, so its peak (E flat 6 to D6) is the highest the violins go.

Fugato: a three-bar subject, real answers at the fifth, a countersubject, four entries (violas, second violins, cellos with basses and bassoons, first violins with oboes and flutes) and an episode on the subject's falling cell. A real, not tonal, answer: this is a development, and it should modulate.
The return is prepared by C7 heard as the augmented sixth of E minor and ten bars of dominant pedal.
Parts that share players never sound together (the script checks it): sustained and spiccato strings are separate tracks of the same desks, horns 1-2 are either hn_t or hn12, and so on.

Mix: the bus chain under the rules of version 2 with wide dynamics (no compression), every part in the hall at its stage depth with one send. mix.c80_db is 2: the brief asks that the singing theme sound as from a good seat in the hall, so the clarity is set inside the range Barron (2013) recommends for concert halls (-2 to +2 dB), at its clear end because of the fugato and the fast low-string figure.
Style: orchestral/romantic. Tempo and rhythm are the piece's own choices where the map gives no source.

Review, minor seconds and ninths (about 150 pairs): kept, all three are written tensions. (1) Bars 90-95: C over the dominant pedal B - the turn's upper note, then the ninth of B7b9 beating against its root before the return. (2) Bars 119-120: F in the trumpets over the tonic pedal E, the Neapolitan against the tonic; E is kept out of every part but the bass register there. (3) The figure's C against a held B is the neighbour note the whole piece is built on. Each counts once for every pair of doubling parts. The accidental ones the first reviews found (woodwind lines a semitone from held chord notes at bars 47, 50, 73-77, 84-85, 113) were rewritten.

Review, parallel octaves (about 160 pairs): kept, they are doublings. 118 of the pairs are the gesture's B-C in bars 1 and 98, one line played in octaves by twelve parts; the rest are the figure, the themes and the turn doubled between sections, in passages too short for review to read as doublings. The real parallels the first reviews found were rewritten: fifths between violas and second violins at bar 72, octaves between the violas' rocking figure and the violins' run in bars 78-85.

Levels: every part is levelled by its peak (its loudest moment), set from the measured stems of rounds 1-5, so the tutti balance follows the orchestration guide (brass over strings over woodwinds) and soft passages follow their written dynamics.

mix.range_lu 13: the piece will be heard on ordinary speakers more than in a hall; the natural range measured 17 LU, with the bridge and the codetta 15-16 LU under the return. The loudest passages keep their level.
Violins: +1.5 dB at 5 kHz and +2.5 dB at 9 kHz, the only equalisation in the mix; the sampled sections and horns leave the dry mix with almost nothing above 6 kHz.
